depth_eval_summary.method: Full default eval_depth.main CLI through runpy; --all, stride1, no max frames, min_depth0.001m, no max depth or crop. NPY predictions from depth_maps/da3_metric_large_cpu_float32.
depth_eval_summary.wrapper_note: All scorer outputs were written successfully. The temporary stdout Tee wrapper emitted an interpreter-shutdown warning after closing its log; the CSV cohorts and numeric aggregates were checked independently, without rerunning inference or scoring.

temporal_summary.error_definition: absolute(target_prediction_z - source_prediction_transformed_z); relative denominator source_prediction_transformed_z. GT source/target depth determines correspondence/visibility when present.
temporal_summary.aggregation: Error means/medians/p90 give every finite pair equal weight. Each pair p90 summarizes retained pixels in that pair; its aggregate is not a pooled pixel p90. Coverage pools counts. Missing-pose rows have n_sampled=0 in CSV and count only in nominal-all-pair coverage.
warnings: Temporal consistency measures repeatability, not depth accuracy. A temporally consistent scale bias can have a small score.
KITTI geometry and visibility are prediction-derived, so retained correspondences depend on network error; large background errors may be rejected as occluded.

KITTI supplied poses match the original rectified cam0 reference while pixels/intrinsics are image_2 (cam2); no cam0-to-cam2 extrinsic is supplied. Constant camera-origin offset changes relative translation when rotating; KITTI reprojection is approximate.

TUM nearest RGB/depth association is within 20ms, can reuse a depth image, and uses RGB-timestamp poses without compensating the depth timestamp. Unmatched GT falls back to prediction geometry/visibility and is separated by mode.
Nearest-pixel correspondence, sparse source z-buffer and 0.05m + 5% visibility tolerance are approximations; boundaries, moving objects, depth holes and disocclusions affect retained coverage.
Different scenes/frame intervals/GT masks prevent reading these sequence results as a model ranking.
Evaluation poses and sensor depth are used only for offline scoring, not network inference or online scale.

spatial_diagnostics.aggregation: Pool valid sampled pixels separately within each sequence and region; AbsRel=sum(abs(pred-GT)/GT)/N; RMSE=sqrt(sum((pred-GT)^2)/N); signed error=pred-GT. Exact pooled median of signed errors stored as float32 for the median calculation. These are pixel-pooled metrics, unlike the dense evaluator frame-macro means.
limitations: GT-based discontinuity detection uses a chosen absolute/relative jump threshold and a7x7band; conclusions depend on these settings.
Depth-bin distributions and regional errors reflect64selected frames and their valid GT support, not every frame or all image pixels.
TUM has sensor holes and nearest-timestamp GT associations. Valid-pair edge detection does not interpret holes as depth edges.
No network inference, scale fitting, correction, cache changes or GT-driven model input was performed.
Outside the detected band does not mean geometrically flat. Thresholded spatial statistics alone do not establish semantic failure causes.

provenance.computation: one-off inline diagnostic; no project scripts modified

limitations: KITTI 06 has no supplied GT depth, so no KITTI depth accuracy is claimed.
TUM uses nearest GT depth within 20 ms; unmatched RGB frames are excluded from depth scores and sensor holes are masked.
KITTI temporal geometry/visibility is prediction-dependent and uses the supplied reference-pose stream without an explicit cam0-to-colour-cam2 extrinsic correction.
Temporal consistency does not establish metric accuracy; moving objects and sensor timing can affect it.
ORB keypoints are diagnostic detections, not the saved SLAM observations; patch dispersion is an uncalibrated uncertainty heuristic.
Full inference and these diagnostics do not by themselves finish the actual SLAM-keypoint/map-scale requirements or Part 3 integrations.
